feedback: The confession follows the exact chronological discrepancy available before voting, so the central solution feels earned. Monet explicitly confirms the after-preview visit, poison taking and application, but these supply the admitted actions rather than a new external clue needed to identify her. Her distinction between wages already paid and the threatened rescue gives the motive emotional specificity; the final acknowledgment of Grant's family prevents payroll anxiety from excusing murder. Elle's and Chip's separate admissions also pay off their contradictory records without making every lie homicidal. The ending remains concise enough to work after a long evidence round. I would still describe the pre-vote case as a strong inference from a specific cover-story failure rather than forensic exclusion of every alternative.
